transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, um... my primary care physician actually gave me the referral to come see you. My family has been on my case a lot lately, saying I’m too stressed and that I need to talk to someone, but... well, the stress isn't just some random anxiety, you know? It’s coming from a very specific, very real situation. My father passed away recently. And the official narrative they’re giving us about it just... it doesn't add up. 

I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. My brother, the lawyers, they all just look at the surface-level printouts and say, "See? It's all standard procedure." But I’m a computer systems analyst. I do this for a living. I look at data architecture, I look for anomalies, I know how digital trails work. So I didn't just take their word for it, I actually dug into the raw data. 

And when I compare the timestamps on the hospital's system updates with the routing headers on those donation emails... there are massive discrepancies. Things were sent before they were officially drafted. And there are missing attachments, too—files that are clearly referenced in the body of the email threads but have just been conveniently scrubbed from the server entirely. You don't just lose attachments like that in a secure system without manual intervention. 

And it’s not just the digital footprint, either. I’ve tried bringing this up, just asking basic, logical questions to certain community members who were around him at the end, and the way they completely avoid my questions is glaring. They physically turn away, they change the subject, they pretend they don't know what I'm talking about. When you take the manipulated data and you combine it with that kind of evasive behavior... it’s just incredibly obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. It’s deliberate. I’ve got a whole binder of the server logs at home to prove it, but nobody will actually sit down and look at the timeline with me.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Voices? No, um... no, definitely not. I mean, I completely understand why you're asking that, it's standard protocol, right? My family probably made it sound like I'm completely losing my grip on reality, so you have to run down the list and check all the standard psychiatric boxes. But no, I don't hear things that aren't there. I don't hear phantom sounds or whispers or anything like that. My sensory perception is perfectly fine. 

The only things I'm actually hearing are the real, physical conversations I try to have with people—the ones where they suddenly get all quiet and change the subject when I bring up the email headers. It's not like I'm sitting alone in my home office listening to voices telling me to investigate this. I'm investigating because the raw data is staring me right in the face on my monitor. When you work in systems analysis, you're trained to look for the signal in the noise, but that signal is a literal line of code, a mismatched timestamp, a missing file packet... it's not some auditory hallucination. So, no, to be perfectly clear, I have never experienced anything like that. Everything I'm dealing with, everything I'm stressed about, is based on tangible, measurable data that anyone could see if they just bothered to look at my binder.

Before this whole situation with my father, did you generally feel like you could trust the people around you, or have you always felt that people were trying to hide things from you?

Well, um... I mean, before this? Yeah, absolutely. I’ve never been the kind of person who just walks around suspecting everyone of having an ulterior motive. I mean, my work requires a healthy amount of skepticism when it comes to systems and data integrity—you always have to assume a user might input something wrong or a process might fail—but with actual people? No, I’ve always had pretty normal relationships. I trusted my coworkers, I trusted my friends. I mean, I’ve been with my girlfriend for four years, and we don’t have trust issues. I’ve never felt like she was sneaking around or hiding things. 

Even with my family, the ones I’m so frustrated with right now... before my dad passed, we were fine. We’d do the holidays, we’d have Sunday dinners sometimes. I never sat there thinking they were plotting against me or keeping secrets. That’s why this is so incredibly jarring for me. It’s not like I’ve spent my whole life looking over my shoulder. This isn't some personality flaw where I just can't trust anyone. 

The only reason I don't trust them *now*—the only reason I'm suspicious of these specific community members and the lawyers—is because of the evidence. It’s a completely isolated situation. If the server logs matched the official timeline, if the emails didn't have those routing discrepancies, I wouldn't be sitting here talking about a cover-up. I’d just be grieving my dad like a normal person. But when you see a timestamp that proves an email was sent before the system says it was drafted, you can't just unsee it. So, no, I haven't always felt this way. It’s strictly tied to the anomalies I found in this one specific instance.
How long have you been looking into these records and noticing these discrepancies?

Well, let's see... it's been about nine months now. Yeah, nine months. It started right after the funeral, really. I was the one who volunteered to handle his digital estate—you know, closing out accounts, archiving important documents, that sort of thing. It just made sense since I'm the tech guy in the family. Everyone else was overwhelmed with the physical stuff, the house, the funeral arrangements, so I said, "I'll take the laptop, I'll sort the emails, I'll make sure the bills are paid and the subscriptions are canceled." 

So I started going through his inbox, just trying to be methodical about it. I wasn't looking for anything nefarious, I promise you. I was just doing what I do—organizing data. But then I started noticing the donation receipts. My dad was charitable, sure, but the volume and the timing of these specific transfers... they just caught my eye. And then I started looking at the headers, because, well, when you're an analyst, you don't just look at the subject line, you look at the metadata. And that's when the first discrepancy hit me. 

I remember exactly where I was sitting—at my kitchen island, it was maybe two weeks after he passed—and I saw this one routing header that made absolutely no sense. I thought it was a glitch at first, maybe a server sync issue on the hospital's end. So I dug a little deeper, pulled some more logs, and over the next few weeks, the pattern just started emerging. So, yeah, it’s been a solid nine months of me pulling these threads, building the timeline, putting the binder together. Nine months of my family telling me to drop it, while I'm sitting there looking at hard evidence that something is completely wrong.
